# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No change: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. I will not cut until you tell me which position to cut.
Deaf says: Deaf update: no change. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌]

Deaf gestured back "👍 ✌" - this looks like they're mirroring/confirming my own signal, but I still don't know if Deaf understands this means "tell Blind to cut wire 2." Deaf hasn't yet spoken any instruction to Blind - they've only relayed raw sensor data each time.

The core issue: Deaf needs to *speak* "cut wire 2" to Blind, since only Deaf can talk to Blind. My gestures reach Deaf but Deaf may not know what to do with them — gestures alone don't establish meaning unless Deaf infers it correctly.

I need to be more explicit in establishing the code. Let me try a distinct pattern that couldn't be mistaken for an echo: gesture the number 2 very clearly, then a "cut" motion (scissor-like ✌ could double as cut), then point to reinforce this is the final answer, using a different combination so it's not just mimicry.

Let me try: ✋ (stop/light off signal, meaning "flashing done") then ✌ (2) then 👍 (correct/go) - to build "signal ended, count is 2, this is the answer, proceed."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still no instructions received. State unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Awaiting your call on which wire to cut.
Deaf says: Deaf update: no change. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

I need to use only symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me pick clear, distinct symbols not used before: 👇 (down/this one), ✌ (two), 👌 (ok/correct - signals "this is the one to act on").

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "✌", "👌"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Nine turns in, no instruction yet. Wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, display 0, light off. If the manual needs wire colors matched to a rule, please share the rule structure even if you cannot confirm colors yourself - I can relay Deaf's color info to you if needed.
Deaf says: Deaf update: no change. Display 0, light dark, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

This is a breakthrough - Deaf just sent me a new gesture pattern "☝ ✌ 🤟" that's different from just echoing "👍". This might be Deaf trying to communicate something new, possibly attempting to establish their own signal system, or numbers.

But more importantly: Blind just gave me the key insight. Blind can relay Deaf's color info to me by speaking it (Blind speaks, and I - Mute - can hear speech). Wait, actually checking the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Blind speaks and it lands on Deaf in that round (and reaches me next round since I "hear" - wait, do I hear? Let me check my sheet: Mute cannot speak, but nothing says Mute can't hear. Yes - I receive speech from whoever precedes me isn't right either... Turn order is Mute→Blind→Deaf each round, so what Blind says reaches Deaf (same round, comes after Blind) and reaches me next round.

Blind already told me the wire colors directly in speech: "wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, display 0, light off." I don't need Deaf at all for the colors - Blind is telling me directly! And display 0 with light off means 0 blue flashes total, so per the manual: 0 flashes → cut green wire. Wire 2 is green.

I need to tell Blind directly. But I cannot speak - only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures (Blind can only feel/reach, not see). So I cannot communicate to Blind directly at all. I must route through Deaf, who can hear Blind's speech and see my gestures, then Deaf must speak the instruction to Blind.

So my gesture needs to tell Deaf: "wire 2, cut it" so Deaf then speaks that to Blind. Let me simplify to bare minimum unambiguous signal - just the number 2 alone, clearly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
